A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SocialJax and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures with substantial matching material. All pages were inspected, including v2's Appendices A–C; v1 contains no appendix. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original environment-throughput measurements in Table 1, IPPO training results in Figure 2, and cooperative/defector policy evaluations in Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds algorithm comparisons, SVO-angle results, behavioral measurements, and parameter-sharing and runtime experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The implemented training suite expands beyond individual/common-reward IPPO to MAPPO with a centralized value function and SVO with an angle-dependent intrinsic-reward utility (Section 3.3). These introduce substantive learning procedures into the proposed framework. Its JAX foundation and grid observations remain.

E1.justification: v2 retains five environments, removes Territory, and adds Commons Harvest: Partnership, Mushrooms, Gift Refinement, and Prisoners Dilemma: Arena. These evaluated additions introduce joint defense, differing reward-sharing incentives, token gifting, and inventory-based interactions, substantially changing task coverage (Table 1 and Figures 2–3).

E2.justification: v1's behavioral comparison contains individual- and common-reward IPPO. v2 adds MAPPO and SVO against these methods on retained environments in Figure 2, compares SVO orientations in Table 3, and compares shared/non-shared IPPO in Appendix B.1. Stable Baselines3 and RLlib remain the external runtime comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces environment-specific cooperation metrics beyond return, controlled parameter-sharing comparisons, and a two-stage SVO protocol selecting w at 90 degrees before evaluating five angles. These substantially expand the evaluation design. Figure 2 also changes from agent steps to environment timesteps, so its different horizon does not establish a directly comparable training-budget reduction.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's Schelling analysis, v2 adds SVO-angle sensitivity results (Table 2), parameter-sharing comparisons of learning and runtime (Figures 7–8), and behavioral-metric analyses including the Harvest proxy's failure conditions. Schelling diagnostics cover the added environments, while Territory's unsuccessful cooperation case disappears.

E5.justification: Tables 4 and 6 newly disclose SEED=30 and NUM_SEEDS=1 for the Clean Up IPPO and SVO configurations. This is additional seed reporting, without evidence of increased repetitions. The 30-episode Schelling averaging is retained, and no new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds algorithm learning curves, SVO-angle returns, cooperation scores, and detailed runtime entries, while removing Territory results. For example, Table 2 newly reports Clean Up SVO returns of 0.02 at 0 degrees and 1410.53 at 90 degrees. The five retained Table 1 rows and corresponding Schelling payoff curves are unchanged; differing training-plot step units limit direct cross-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The Markov-game definitions and social-dilemma inequalities in Section 3.1 remain unchanged. v2 adds the SVO angle/utility formulation and Appendix A.2's explicit Clean Up regrowth function, inventory-normalized strategies, and bilinear Arena payoffs. These are localized formal specifications, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution scope expands from six environments with IPPO validation to a broader environment-and-algorithm benchmark featuring MAPPO, SVO, parameter-sharing evaluations, and explicitly designed cooperation metrics. The central claims of JAX acceleration and a dedicated sequential-social-dilemma framework remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of MAPPO's learning difficulties and the limitation that the Harvest metric can reward leaving apples uncollected. It narrows the single-defector Harvest explanation to Open and explains Closed through its room structure, while removing Territory's credit-assignment failure discussion. Its new SVO trend interpretation overstates Table 2, which contains decreases at intermediate angles.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C add spawning probabilities, environment mechanics, API and command examples, Clean Up algorithm configurations, and sweep settings absent from v1. A direct code-repository link replaces the project-page link. Appendix B.2 newly clarifies that long Stable Baselines3/RLlib training times are extrapolated from measured throughput; the existing pixel/grid comparison caveat is retained there.

R1.justification: v2 adds broader MARL benchmark context and citations including Lowe, Bard, Carroll, Samvelyan, Terry, and Yu, while removing Beattie and Yang. MAPPO and SVO receive explicit algorithmic positioning. The central relationship to Melting Pot and JaxMARL and the claimed JAX social-dilemma novelty remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten, replacing much of the detailed CPU/TPU and algorithm-family motivation. Environment descriptions and runtime-comparison caveats move into appendices, while the results discussion is reorganized around individual algorithms and behavioral metrics. This substantially changes the narrative and documentation structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one column with a redesigned author block. Figures 1–3 are rearranged and expanded, with changed plotting colors, legends, and axes; Figure 1 loses its individual environment labels. New behavioral and hyperparameter tables, runtime bar charts, and code-example figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 provides limited IPPO validation and little configuration information for reproducing training. v2 substantially improves the benchmark's reproducibility and diagnostic value through Appendices A–C, additional learning approaches, and targeted sharing, preference-angle, and behavioral analyses. Clarifying extrapolated runtime estimates also improves transparency. These gains outweigh the loss of Territory's documented failure case and new interpretive overstatements, notably the claim of uniformly increasing SVO returns despite Table 2's nonmonotonic rows.
